verdict.rationale: Pandoc's own docs cover all three self-hosted deployment modes. It ships as a Haskell library, it has an official pandoc/latex container image, and it can be compiled with an HTTP server mode (pandoc-server). It can also be built as a fully self-contained binary, so it runs entirely on infrastructure the developer controls. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of the server mode's operation and API (the evidence only shows a compile flag), and independent or hands-on corroboration of library, container or server deployments.

support.subject: As a developer, the conversion engine runs inside my own infrastructure as a library, container, or server I operate

citations.quote: Pandoc includes a Haskell library and a standalone command-line program.
The pandoc/latex image also contains the minimal LaTeX installation needed to produce PDFs using pandoc.
server: compile in support for running in HTTP server mode when the executable is renamed (or symlinked as) pandoc-server.
The resulting binary can be run from any directory and is completely self-contained.
